title: Whitegate Way Circular Walk Route

images.title: Whitegate Way looking South past the picnic area by Dr Duncan Pepper, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Whitegate Way looking South past the picnic area. The Whitegate Way is a picturesque six-mile rail trail in Cheshire that follows the route of a former railway line originally built to transport salt from the mines at Winsford. Stretching from the heart of Winsford to Cuddington, the path offers a flat, traffic-free corridor through the countryside that is ideal for cyclists of all abilities. The route is characterised by its smooth surface and gentle gradients, making it particularly popular for families and those looking for a relaxed ride away from the noise of main roads.

images.title: Hut beside the Whitegate Way by Stephen Craven, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Nature has reclaimed much of the old trackbed, and the route is now flanked by a diverse mix of woodland and local wildlife habitats. As you cycle along the trail, you pass through a variety of landscapes including shaded cuttings and open embankments that offer elevated views over the surrounding Cheshire farmland. The Way is also a haven for birdlife and wild flowers, providing a seasonal backdrop that changes from bluebells in the spring to rich autumnal colours later in the year.

images.title: Raymond Knapman / The former Whitegate station house
images.caption: The former Whitegate station house. A key highlight for many visitors is the Station House at Whitegate, located roughly halfway along the route. This restored Victorian station serves as a convenient stopping point with a car park, toilets, and a popular cafe where cyclists can break for refreshments. The trail also links up with the wider network of paths in the area, including the Delamere Forest tracks and the Weaver Valley, allowing more ambitious cyclists to extend their journey into the neighbouring woodlands and river valleys.

description: This route uses sections of the Whitegate Way and the Weaver Way to create a fine circular walk through the Cheshire countryside. Starting at the Whitegate Way car park the route first heads north east through Foxtwist Green and Whitegate to meet with the River Weaver Navigation at the photogenic Vale Royal Locks. You then follow the waterside path south east towards Moulton before rejoining the Whitegate Way to complete the circuit. The trail runs for about 7.6 miles and is mostly flat.
